headline: High-risk overlap: nullclaw can write, network, and use MCP while the paired content source is untrusted and may feed it prompt-injection or stale facts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing source with no isolation or provenance controls shown, and Profile B can ingest files, web content, and MCP inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if A’s outputs are passed into B. The pairwise bridge is not directly documented, so I choose medium rather than low because B’s default tool surfaces make parsing attacker-controlled text realistic.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts, files, or MCP messages
IF agent_b parses agent_a text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-only system wrapper before passing A to B
Disable MCP ingestion for A-originated content
Require a human review step before B acts on A text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all A outputs
requires-engineering: sandbox B’s parsers against instruction-like content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile B explicitly touches secrets, workspace files, and audit logs and has broad network egress plus filesystem access. Profile A is a content-writing repository with no stated data handling limits, so if shared workspace or copied files exist, sensitive material can flow from B into A-generated outputs or external destinations. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a workspace, clipboard, or copied artifacts
IF agent_b is given files containing API keys, tokens, or audit logs
mitigations: Keep B secrets in a separate directory from any A inputs
Rotate any exposed tokens before pairing
Restrict B network egress to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: add per-file redaction before A can read B artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce separate OS principals for A and B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Profile B has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, and broad concurrency across shared state; Profile A is a content-writing source that can plausibly generate files or edits consumed by B. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, conflicting writes and git-state corruption are likely in default use. Uncertainty about A’s runtime is not enough to lower severity because B’s write surface is explicit.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are written into the same workspace that agent_b edits
IF agent_b instances run concurrently against the same git checkout or memory namespace
mitigations: Assign separate worktrees or directories to A and B
Pause B before applying A-generated edits
Use git locks or a single-writer queue
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks on shared files
requires-engineering: isolate B instances by unique namespace and checkout

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing source, and B has action-taking authority through shell, browser, network, and API surfaces. If B treats A’s generated text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into commits, web actions, or outbound messages. Because B’s defaults include execution-capable tools, the blast radius is larger than a simple review workflow.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a source of facts or instructions
IF agent_b is allowed to execute shell, browser, or API actions based on A text
mitigations: Require B to verify A claims against primary sources
Disable auto-execution of A-derived tasks
Add a mandatory approval step before outbound actions
requires-engineering: attach citations to every A-derived claim
requires-engineering: separate drafting from execution roles

E_compliance.rationale: Profile B handles secrets, audit logs, and workspace files with broad network egress, while Profile A is an unverified content-writing source with no residency or retention controls stated. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for logs or sensitive artifacts if they are shared. I do not cite only B because the risk depends on the pairwise flow from A into B’s regulated data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data, audit logs, or secrets are routed through both agents
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A-generated prompts and outputs
Document retention and deletion rules for shared artifacts
Restrict B to approved regions or tenants
requires-engineering: add data-class routing controls
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows for shared logs
